original.target_description: Experiment 3: right-handed participants; paired-samples comparison of perceived/actual left versus right hand area, computed from length × width, not hand length alone.

n.exclusions: One of the 15 recruited participants removed for misunderstanding instructions.
n.location: pp. 1376–1377, Experiment 3 Participants and Results and Discussion
n.quote: Fifteen right-handed (6 female and 9 male) University of Virginia students participated in Experiment 3; One participant’s data were removed from the analysis because he indicated that he misunderstood the instructions; t(13)

es.location: p. 1377, Experiment 3 Results and Discussion, hand-size accuracy paragraph
es.quote: Participants underestimated the size of their left hand (M = 0.91, SD = 0.19) more than the size of their right hand (M = 0.99, SD = 0.18), t(13) = 3.03, prep = .97, ηp² = .41.

p.location: p. 1377, Experiment 3 Results and Discussion, hand-size accuracy paragraph

replication.target_description: Experiment 1: right-handed participants’ categorical judgments of which hand is larger; chi-square goodness-of-fit on initial right-versus-left answers, excluding same-size responses. This measures overall hand size, not hand length.

n.sample_role: right-handed participants providing an initial right-or-left hand-size judgment in the chi-square test
n.exclusions: 15 of 50 initially answered about the same size and were not included in the initial test; they were included in a separately reported forced-choice analysis.
n.location: p. 751, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion, initial-question analysis
n.quote: A chi-square test of goodness-of-fit for the participants who responded right (n = 25) and left (n = 10) to the first question showed a significant difference, χ²(1, N = 35) = 6.4, p < .001.

es.location: p. 751, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion, initial-question analysis

p.location: p. 751, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion, initial-question analysis

reported_success.location: p. 751, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion, concluding sentence
reported_success.quote: This supports the claim made by Linkenauger et al. (2009) that most right-handed observers perceive their right hand as larger than their left hand.

notes: Original target description specifies hand length, but the located Experiment 3 test compares perceived/actual hand area. No conventional p value is printed for this test; p_rep = .97 is a replication probability, not a p value. Replication Experiment 1 measures categorical hand size rather than length, hence target_match=false on both sides. The initial-question test is recorded because it is the first reported test for this outcome. A separate analysis adds forced-choice answers from the 15 initially equal-size respondents and reports χ²(1, N = 50) = 15.7, p < .001 (p. 751). The locator does not distinguish these two analyses. Replication p is retained exactly as printed, without recomputation. The authors’ successful verdict concerns the broader hand-size claim, not an exact replication of a hand-length measurement. Original analytic n=14 is established by 15 recruited minus one explicitly excluded and corroborated by t(13).
